name: NoniHours – Business Hours Status
author: muse1990

sections.description:
NoniHours is a small, focused plugin that answers one question for your visitors: “Are you open right now?”

Set your opening and closing time for each day of the week under Settings > NoniHours, then place the shortcodes anywhere on your site — a header, a sidebar, your contact page, or your footer.

Shortcodes

  • [open_hours_status] — Shows the current status using your own wording, plus today’s hours. Example output: “Open now · 9:00–18:00”. The status is calculated from the timezone in your WordPress settings (Settings > General), so it is always correct for your business location, not the visitor’s.
  • [open_hours_week] — Shows the full weekly hours list, Monday to Sunday, with today highlighted.

Features

  • Opening and closing time per weekday, with a “closed all day” option per day
  • Custom “Open now” and “Closed” texts — use any wording or language you like
  • Uses your WordPress timezone and time format settings
  • Lightweight: no external requests, no tracking, no ads, nothing leaves your site
  • Translation-ready
sections.installation:
1. Upload the nonihours-business-hours-status folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings > NoniHours and set your weekly hours.
  4. Add [open_hours_status] and/or [open_hours_week] to any post, page, widget, or template.
sections.faq:
Which timezone does the status use?

Your site’s timezone, as set in Settings > General > Timezone. NoniHours reads it through WordPress itself (wp_timezone()), so daylight saving changes are handled automatically.

Can I set overnight hours, such as 18:00–02:00?

Not in this version. NoniHours supports same-day ranges only (for example 9:00–18:00). A range whose closing time is earlier than its opening time will simply never show as open.

What happens on a day I mark “Closed all day”?

The status shortcode shows only your “Closed” text for that day, and the weekly list shows “Closed” instead of a time range.

Can I change the “Open now” and “Closed” wording?

Yes. Both texts can be changed on the settings page, so you can write them in your own language or style, for example “We’re open — come on in!”.

Does the plugin collect any data or phone home?

No. NoniHours makes no external network requests and contains no tracking or analytics. Your hours are stored in a single WordPress option.

How can I style the output?

The shortcodes output semantic HTML with CSS classes you can target: .ophrs-status, .ophrs-status--open, .ophrs-status--closed, .ophrs-week, .ophrs-day, and .ophrs-day--today. A small default stylesheet (a colored open/closed dot and a simple list layout) is included and can be overridden by your theme.

1.0.0

  • Weekly opening hours settings page under Settings > NoniHours.
  • [open_hours_status] shortcode with live open/closed status based on the site timezone.
  • [open_hours_week] shortcode with the full weekly hours list.
